# Architecture catalog

Evidence catalog date: 2026-10-15. For changing B2 product details, use <https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-ai-machine-learning> as the authority.

## Voice training data lifecycle

Collect speech with consent, validate and review it, and publish immutable dataset releases that NeMo, Lhotse, Hugging Face Datasets, WebDataset and MosaicML Streaming read from B2.

**Use when:** Speech datasets need a record of consent per clip, repeatable validation, reviewed transcripts and versioned releases that training jobs in other locations can read and cite exactly.

**Workflow:** Record consent in the protected zone -> Upload clips with presigned PUT URLs -> Validate and normalize on signed Event Notifications -> Review transcripts in Label Studio -> Build an immutable release with manifests and shards -> Read the release through a local cache for training

**B2 capabilities:** S3-compatible API, Presigned URLs and CORS, Multipart upload with resume, Application keys with limited scope, Event Notifications with a signed, idempotent webhook, Versions and lifecycle rules, Server-side encryption, Object Lock, Cloud Replication, Included egress and compute partners, Local processing or GPU cache, B2 Overdrive for sustained reads only.

**Integrations:** [NVIDIA NeMo](https://docs.nvidia.com/nemo-framework/user-guide/latest/nemotoolkit/asr/datasets.html) (application copies data to or from b2): Reads releases through its Lhotse data loader, or from a local copy; its own object-store support is documented for AIStore; [Lhotse](https://github.com/lhotse-speech/lhotse) (provider uses an s3-compatible endpoint): Shard sources given as pipe commands with an S3 client and the B2 endpoint, or as s3 URIs opened through smart_open; [WebDataset](https://github.com/webdataset/webdataset) (provider uses an s3-compatible endpoint): Shard URLs as pipe commands with an S3 client and the B2 endpoint, or presigned https URLs read with curl; [Hugging Face Datasets](https://huggingface.co/docs/datasets/package_reference/loading_methods) (provider uses an s3-compatible endpoint): storage_options passed to the s3fs backend with the B2 endpoint_url; [MosaicML Streaming](https://docs.mosaicml.com/projects/streaming/en/stable/how_to_guides/configure_cloud_storage_credentials.html) (provider uses an s3-compatible endpoint): S3_ENDPOINT_URL set to the B2 S3 endpoint; remote s3 path and local cache directory; [Label Studio](https://labelstud.io/guide/storage_s3) (provider uses an s3-compatible endpoint): Amazon S3 storage type with the S3 endpoint field set to B2; source storage with pre-signed URLs and target storage for annotations; [MLflow](https://mlflow.org/docs/latest/self-hosting/architecture/artifact-store/) (provider uses an s3-compatible endpoint): Artifact root on an s3 path with MLFLOW_S3_ENDPOINT_URL set to the B2 S3 endpoint; [DVC](https://doc.dvc.org/user-guide/data-management/remote-storage/amazon-s3) (provider uses an s3-compatible endpoint): S3 remote with endpointurl set to the B2 S3 endpoint.

**Scale:** From thousands of clips to multi-terabyte speech corpora. Collection and review run at any scale on standard B2. Training reads go through a local cache; B2 Overdrive applies only when sustained aggregate read throughput is the measured constraint.

**Security:** One application key per component and prefix, read-only and expiring for training jobs; Presigned PUT URLs for one object with a short expiry; Webhook signature verified on the raw body and each eventId processed once; SSE-B2 default encryption; object names and metadata carry pseudonymous ids only; CORS limited to the contributor app and Label Studio origins.

**Evidence basis:** Third-party behavior checked against each tool's official documentation or source code on 2026-10-15; B2 behavior checked against the Backblaze documentation linked from the capability map; Release manifest example validated against its schema and recomputed from the synthetic fixtures in CI; Application tests run in CI against an emulated S3 server, not against a B2 account or the named tools.

## Batch voice generation and dubbing

Send sources to dubbing, speech synthesis and transcription providers through presigned GET URLs, keep every output as an expiring candidate, and promote reviewed outputs to immutable deliveries with lineage.

**Use when:** Batch dubbing, speech synthesis and transcription jobs produce many outputs from hosted providers that return results through their own APIs; each output needs review, unused outputs must expire, and every delivered file must trace back to its source, job and consent.

**Workflow:** Upload the source to the incoming zone -> Start a job on a signed Event Notification and check consent -> Submit the job with a presigned GET URL sized to the provider's download window -> Collect outputs on callback or by polling and copy them to candidates -> Review candidates through short-lived presigned URLs -> Promote approved outputs to an immutable delivery version with lineage -> Deliver through short-lived URLs or a private CDN while candidates expire

**B2 capabilities:** S3-compatible API, Presigned URLs and CORS, Multipart upload with resume, Application keys with limited scope, Event Notifications with a signed, idempotent webhook, Versions and lifecycle rules, Server-side encryption, Object Lock, Cloud Replication, Private delivery through a CDN, Delivery through compute partners, Local processing or GPU cache.

**Integrations:** [ElevenLabs Dubbing](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/dubbing/create-project) (application copies data to or from b2): Reads the source from a presigned GET URL passed as source_url; the application downloads the dubbed audio and subtitles from the signed output URLs and writes them to B2; [Deepgram](https://developers.deepgram.com/docs/pre-recorded-audio) (application copies data to or from b2): Reads the source from a presigned GET URL in the url field; the transcript returns in the response or by callback and the application writes it to B2; [AssemblyAI](https://www.assemblyai.com/docs/api-reference/transcripts/submit) (application copies data to or from b2): Reads the source from a presigned GET URL passed as audio_url; the application fetches the transcript after the webhook or by polling and writes it to B2; [Cloudflare CDN](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-deliver-private-backblaze-b2-content-through-cloudflare-cdn) (provider uses an s3-compatible endpoint): A Cloudflare Worker signs each request to the private releases bucket's S3 endpoint with an application key scoped to deliveries.

**Scale:** From a few jobs a day to continuous batches of dubbing and transcription. Throughput is bound by the providers' job limits and the runner's concurrency, not by B2. Each output is stored at least twice while a candidate and its delivery coexist; candidate lifecycle bounds that overlap.

**Security:** One presigned GET URL per job and object version, signed just before submission; hosted providers never receive a key; Presigned URL lifetime longer than the provider's download window and recorded in the job manifest, never the URL itself; Provider callbacks verified by signature or configured credentials and handled idempotently; One application key per component and prefix; delivery keys read-only and scoped to deliveries; SSE-B2 default encryption; object names and metadata carry job ids and pseudonymous speaker ids only.

**Evidence basis:** Provider behavior checked against ElevenLabs, Deepgram and AssemblyAI documentation on 2026-10-15; B2 behavior checked against the Backblaze documentation linked from the capability map; Generation job manifest example validated against its schema in CI; Application tests run in CI against an emulated S3 server, not against a B2 account or the providers.

## Voice agent session archive

Archive finished voice agent sessions from LiveKit Egress or a session adapter, evaluate each session for quality and safety, retain it per class under Object Lock, and select only passed, consented sessions for review, analytics or datasets.

**Use when:** Voice agent platforms produce recordings, tracks, transcripts and events that must be kept for a defined period, traced to consent, and checked before anyone reuses them; most platforms do not write to B2 themselves.

**Workflow:** Record the session with LiveKit Egress to B2, or copy it from the platform with an adapter -> Write the session manifest last, when the session has ended -> Start evaluation on a signed Event Notification for the manifest -> Run quality and safety checks and record the result and eligible uses -> Copy sessions to the protected zone with retention per class -> Retrieve sessions through short-lived presigned URLs issued by the application -> Select passed sessions whose consent covers the use into dataset releases

**B2 capabilities:** S3-compatible API, Presigned URLs and CORS, Multipart upload with resume, Application keys with limited scope, Event Notifications with a signed, idempotent webhook, Versions and lifecycle rules, Server-side encryption, Object Lock, Cloud Replication, Local processing or GPU cache.

**Integrations:** [LiveKit Egress](https://docs.livekit.io/home/egress/outputs/) (provider uses an s3-compatible endpoint): S3 output with the B2 endpoint, force_path_style and a key limited to sessions/ in the incoming bucket; template in infrastructure/livekit-egress; [Pipecat](https://docs.pipecat.ai/server/utilities/audio/audio-buffer-processor) (application copies data to or from b2): AudioBufferProcessor hands mixed or per-track PCM to the application, which converts it and uploads it to B2; [Twilio Voice](https://www.twilio.com/docs/voice/api/recording) (application copies data to or from b2): The recording status callback triggers the adapter, which downloads the media with HTTP Basic authentication and writes it to B2; Twilio external storage supports AWS S3 only; [Daily](https://docs.daily.co/reference/rest-api/recordings/get-recording-link) (application copies data to or from b2): The recording.ready-to-download webhook triggers the adapter, which downloads the file through the recording access link API and writes it to B2; Daily custom storage supports Amazon S3 only, with OCI by request; [Vapi](https://docs.vapi.ai/security-and-privacy/retrieve-call-artifacts) (application copies data to or from b2): After the end-of-call-report event, the adapter fetches recordings from the authenticated artifact endpoints, which redirect to short-lived signed URLs, and writes them to B2.

**Scale:** From a few sessions a day to continuous call volume. Capture and archive scale with the platform's recording throughput, not with B2. Each retained session is stored twice until the incoming copy expires; the incoming lifecycle bounds that overlap.

**Security:** Only the Egress key reaches a platform, limited to sessions/ in the incoming bucket; Platform API credentials kept in the adapter; platform download links fetched server-side and never stored; Event Notification, LiveKit, Twilio and Daily webhooks verified before acting and each event processed once; Retrieval through short-lived presigned GET URLs issued after the application authorizes the person; SSE-B2 default encryption; object names and metadata carry session ids and pseudonymous participant ids only.

**Evidence basis:** Platform behavior checked against LiveKit, Pipecat, Twilio, Daily and Vapi documentation on 2026-10-15; B2 behavior checked against the Backblaze documentation linked from the capability map; Session manifest example and synthetic session fixture validated against their schema in CI; Application tests run in CI against an emulated S3 server and signed sample LiveKit webhooks, not against a B2 account or a LiveKit server.
